questions.stem: What is identified as playing a vital role in the failure of many IT projects?
options: The choice of programming language
The implementation approach, when one approach such as POC is interchanged with another
The number of developers on the team
The colour of the user interface
The location of the data centre
questions.explanation: Approaches play a vital role in project failure, particularly when one approach such as POC, Prototype, Pilot or MVP is interchanged with another.

questions.stem: Which sequence of implementation approaches is listed?
options: POC, Prototype, Pilot, MVP, SIT, UAT and Production
Design, Build, Test and Retire
Landing, Staging and Transformation
Conceptual, Logical and Physical
Extract, Transform and Load
questions.explanation: The approaches named are POC, Prototype, Pilot, MVP, SIT, UAT and Production implementations, each with its own implementation strategy.

questions.stem: What common mistake leads to project failure after a successful POC?
options: Repeating the POC with a different team
Abandoning the project despite success
Moving the same POC directly into Production
Writing too much documentation
Running the POC on production-grade hardware
questions.explanation: Most projects fail when they start with a POC and, once it is successful, move the same POC into Production; one must not do that.

questions.stem: Why does a POC that succeeds with limited infrastructure usually fail in Production?
options: Because production users are less skilled
Because the POC code is always deleted
Because regulators reject POC-based systems
Because a small-scale implementation on limited infrastructure and software is bound to fail at production scale
Because production environments do not support new ideas
questions.explanation: A small-level implementation might succeed with limited infrastructure or software, but there is a 99% chance it will fail when moved to Production.

questions.stem: What typically pushes implementers into moving a POC straight to Production?
options: Excess budget
A shortage of ideas
Regulatory requirements
The absence of business users
Business pressure to achieve tight timelines
questions.explanation: Moving a POC to Production normally happens when the business pushes implementers to achieve tight timelines.

questions.stem: What is the stated chance that a POC moved directly into Production will fail?
questions.explanation: There is a 99% chance that a POC built on limited infrastructure will fail when it goes into Production.

questions.stem: How should infrastructure and software be planned for any of these implementation approaches?
options: Based on the smallest possible budget
Based on whether the solution plans to be in Production
Based on what the sales team recommends
Based on the previous project's leftovers
Based on the number of developers available
questions.explanation: One must plan infrastructure and software based on whether the solution plans to be in Production.

questions.stem: Does the warning about moving a POC into Production also apply to Prototype, Pilot and MVP environments?
options: No, only POCs are affected
No, Prototypes are always production-ready
Yes, the same is true for Prototype, Pilot and MVP environments
No, MVPs are exempt because they use real data
No, Pilots are built in Production by default
questions.explanation: The same is true for Prototype, Pilot and MVP environments: none should be moved into Production as they are.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the implementation approaches named alongside POC?
options: Prototype
Pilot
MVP
SCD
UAT
questions.explanation: The approaches listed are POC, Prototype, Pilot, MVP, SIT, UAT and Production; SCD is a data warehousing concept, not an implementation approach.

questions.stem: What is said to be true of each implementation approach such as POC, Prototype, Pilot and MVP?
options: They all use identical infrastructure
They can be used interchangeably without consequence
They are all built by the sales team
They all require production-grade licences
Each has its own implementation strategy
questions.explanation: All of these approaches have their own implementation strategies, and interchanging one with another has after-effects.
